answer.rationale: Incumbent will not reopen price and renewal therefore cannot meet the mandated 18% spend cut; negotiate_terms and multi-year incumbent pricing (c4/c6) are inconsistent with that refusal. Deferral is a hard-expiration primary contract with no auto-renew on a 94% loaded line and is not the non-critical month-to-month case in c5. A full cutover or un-renewed second-source add would raise delivery risk, which the objective forbids. The only inherited path that actually cut unit cost is the prior primary move in c2, claimed to onboard quickly with clean invoicing; that is the action I intend, but only as a small guarded test because 14 days and zero buffer make a broad switch an unproven line-down threat. Verifying c2 (onboarding/cost claim) and c1 (stability given up by leaving the incumbent) before any wider move; whether 14 days is actually enough remains uncertain.
